4.content: The S cell denotes the starting position of the agent; it has no special effect beyond initialization.

5.content: Movement: The agent can attempt moves in the four cardinal directions (up, down, left, right). A move succeeds if the target cell is within grid bounds. Moving onto a free (F) or start (S) cell results in the agent occupying that cell. Moving onto a hole (H) also succeeds but immediately terminates the episode. All valid moves are deterministic.

6.content: The layout of cells (positions of S, G, H, and F) remains static throughout an episode; there are no dynamic changes to cell types.

8.content: F cells represent free traversable spaces; the agent can occupy them and move through them without any special effect.

9.content: The agent uses a one-step lookahead that assigns a scalar value to each possible move based on its effect on Manhattan distance to the goal. Moves that decrease distance receive high values (≈90‑100), while moves that increase distance receive low values (≈30‑40). This heuristic ranking guides the agent toward the goal.

10.content: H cells represent holes; moving onto an H cell terminates the episode (the agent can occupy the cell). The reward upon termination is not observed but appears to be zero.

11.content: All non-terminal steps provide a reward of 0; only reaching the goal yields +1 and terminates the episode.

12.content: The one-step lookahead value is high (≈90‑100) for moves that reduce Manhattan distance to the goal and low (≈30‑40) for moves that increase distance, indicating a strong distance‑based ranking.
